cards.front: Recall a key point about Property Offences
cards.back: Theft is defined in section 1 of the Theft Act 1968 — the dishonest appropriation of property belonging to another with intention to permanently deprive

cards.front: Recall a key point about Property Offences
cards.back: The actus reus of theft requires appropriation, property and that the property belongs to another

cards.front: Recall a key point about Property Offences
cards.back: Appropriation means assuming the rights of the owner — it includes coming into possession and using or dealing with the property

cards.front: Recall a key point about Property Offences
cards.back: Property includes money and all other property, real (land) or personal, tangible or intangible

cards.front: Recall a key point about Property Offences
cards.back: The mens rea of theft requires dishonesty and intention to permanently deprive the other of the property

cards.front: Recall a key point about Property Offences
cards.back: Burglary under section 9 requires entering a building as a trespasser with intent to steal, inflict GBH or do unlawful damage

cards.front: Recall a key point about Property Offences
cards.back: Robbery under section 8 is theft plus the use or threat of force on a person at the time of or immediately before the theft

cards.front: Recall a key point about Property Offences
cards.back: Fraud under the Fraud Act 2006 includes fraud by false representation, fraud by failing to disclose information and fraud by abuse of position

cards.front: Recall a key point about Property Offences
cards.back: Handling stolen goods under section 29 is receiving, arranging or assisting in the retention of stolen goods knowing or believing them to be stolen

cards.front: Recall a key point about Property Offences
cards.back: Blackmail under section 21 is making an unwarranted demand with menaces with a view to gain or intent to cause loss

cards.front: Recall a key point about Property Offences
cards.back: The Theft Act 1968 replaced the complex old larceny laws but some definitions remain contested — especially 'dishonesty'

cards.front: Recall a key point about Property Offences
cards.back: Maximum sentences vary: theft (7 years), burglary (14 years for domestic), robbery (life imprisonment), fraud (10 years)
